derive/expand: Write the loss out. Minus the log of a fraction is minus the log of the top, plus the log of the bottom: minus s y, the correct option's score, plus the log of the total, T.
derive/dT: Log T reaches s zero through a chain: s zero feeds T, and T feeds log T. T adds up e to every score, and only one of those terms holds s zero. e to the x is its own derivative, so T moves e to the one point eight, about six, times as fast as s zero.
derive/dlog: And log T, the natural log, has slope one over T. T is about ten, so log T moves a tenth as fast as T. A nudge of zero point zero one grows to zero point zero six, then shrinks to zero point zero zero six.
derive/pj: The chain rule multiplies the two: six times a tenth is zero point six, the slope measured before. For any score s j, it is e to the s j, over the total. That is exactly p j.
derive/minus: Minus s y depends only on the correct score: its derivative is minus one when j is y, and zero when j is not y, the slashed equals sign reading “is not”.
derive/together: Add the two: p j, minus the bracket j equals y. The bracket is one when j is y and zero otherwise, so it is p j with one taken away at the correct option. Just the pattern the nudges found.
